questions.question: The WHO (1948) defines health as:

options.D: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity

questions.explanation: Later definitions added the capacity to lead a socially and economically productive life.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Early diagnosis and prompt treatment of a disease is an example of:
questions.explanation: Primordial: prevent risk factors from emerging; primary: health promotion and specific protection; secondary: early detection; tertiary: disability limitation and rehabilitation.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Rehabilitation of a patient after stroke is an example of:
questions.explanation: Tertiary prevention limits disability and restores function.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Immunisation of infants against measles is:
questions.explanation: Vaccination protects before disease occurs.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Which of the following is a mortality indicator of health?
questions.explanation: IMR (deaths of infants under 1 year per 1000 live births) is the most sensitive indicator of socio-economic development and health services.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Infant mortality rate is the number of deaths of children under one year of age per:
questions.explanation: IMR uses live births as denominator; maternal mortality ratio uses 100,000 live births.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Maternal mortality ratio is expressed per:
questions.explanation: Deaths due to pregnancy or within 42 days of termination, from causes related to or aggravated by pregnancy.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) is associated with:

options.A: Primary health care and ‘Health for All by 2000’

questions.explanation: Alma-Ata declared primary health care the key to health for all; the Ottawa Charter (1986) concerns health promotion.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: In India's rural health system, a Primary Health Centre (PHC) typically serves a population of:
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Incidence of a disease refers to:

options.A: The number of NEW cases occurring in a population during a specified period
options.B: All existing cases at a point in time

questions.explanation: Prevalence = all existing cases (old + new); prevalence ≈ incidence × mean duration.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Point prevalence is the number of:

options.A: Existing cases at a specific point in time divided by the population

questions.explanation: Prevalence reflects the burden of chronic diseases.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A disease that is constantly present in a given geographical area is called:
questions.explanation: Epidemic: occurrence clearly in excess of normal expectancy; pandemic: spread over several countries.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A study in which a group exposed to a risk factor and a non-exposed group are followed over time to compare disease outcome is a:
questions.explanation: Cohort studies measure incidence and relative risk; case–control studies start with disease and compare past exposures (odds ratio).
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The measure of association obtained from a case–control study is the:
questions.explanation: Cases and controls are selected on disease status, so incidence cannot be calculated.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The gold-standard design for testing the effectiveness of a treatment is a:
questions.explanation: Randomisation reduces selection bias and balances confounders.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: In a double-blind trial:

options.C: Neither the participants nor the investigators know who receives the intervention

questions.explanation: Blinding reduces observer and participant bias.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The sensitivity of a screening test is the proportion of:

options.A: True positives correctly identified among those who have the disease
options.C: True negatives among those who are healthy

questions.explanation: Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN); specificity = TN/(TN+FP). A highly sensitive test is good for ruling out disease (SnNout).
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A test with high specificity is most useful for:
questions.explanation: SpPin: a positive result on a highly specific test is unlikely to be a false positive.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A disease is suitable for population screening if:

options.B: It is an important health problem with a recognisable latent stage and an effective treatment

questions.explanation: Wilson and Jungner criteria.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Recall bias is most likely to occur in a:
questions.explanation: Cases tend to remember past exposures more completely than controls.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A confounding factor is one that:

options.B: Lies on the causal pathway only
options.C: Is not associated with the outcome
options.D: Is associated with both the exposure and the outcome and distorts their observed relationship

questions.explanation: Control by randomisation, restriction, matching or adjustment.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: In a perfectly symmetrical (normal) distribution:

options.B: Median is greater than the mean
options.C: Mean, median and mode are equal
options.D: Mean is greater than the median

questions.explanation: In positively skewed data mean > median > mode; in negatively skewed mean < median < mode.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The best measure of central tendency for skewed data is the:
questions.explanation: The median is not affected by extreme values.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The standard deviation is a measure of:

options.C: Dispersion (spread) of data around the mean

questions.explanation: SD is the square root of variance; in a normal distribution, mean ± 2 SD includes about 95% of values.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: In a normal distribution, approximately what percentage of values lie within ±1 SD of the mean?
questions.explanation: 68% within ±1 SD, 95% within ±1.96 (≈2) SD, 99.7% within ±3 SD.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A p-value < 0.05 in a hypothesis test indicates that:

options.A: The null hypothesis is certainly true
options.C: The result is statistically significant at the 5% level (probability of a chance finding under H0 is < 5%)

questions.explanation: A significant p-value does not measure the size or clinical importance of the effect.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A type I error occurs when:

options.B: A true null hypothesis is rejected (false positive)
options.D: A false null hypothesis is accepted

questions.explanation: Alpha is the probability of a type I error; type II (beta) is a false negative; power = 1 − beta.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Which test is used to compare the means of TWO independent groups with normally distributed data?
questions.explanation: Non-parametric alternative: Mann–Whitney U; paired data: paired t-test.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The chi-square test is used to analyse:
questions.explanation: Compare proportions in frequency tables; Fisher's exact test for small expected counts.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Analysis of variance (ANOVA) is used to compare means of:
questions.explanation: Post-hoc tests (Tukey, Bonferroni) identify which groups differ.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A Pearson correlation coefficient of −0.9 indicates:
questions.explanation: r ranges from −1 to +1; r² gives the proportion of variance explained.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Blood group is an example of which type of variable?
questions.explanation: Nominal: names without order; ordinal: ranked (muscle grade 0–5); interval: equal intervals no true zero (temperature °C); ratio: true zero (height).
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The Oxford muscle strength grade (0–5) is measured on a(n):
questions.explanation: Grades have rank but unequal intervals, so non-parametric statistics are appropriate.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Selecting every fifth patient from a list after a random start is called:
questions.explanation: Stratified sampling divides the population into homogeneous strata before random selection.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Increasing the sample size in a study will generally:

options.C: Reduce the standard error and increase statistical power

questions.explanation: SE = SD/√n; larger samples give narrower confidence intervals.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A 95% confidence interval for a mean means that:

options.A: If the study were repeated many times, 95% of such intervals would contain the true population mean
options.C: The true mean has a 95% probability of being in any single interval after it has been calculated, with certainty
options.D: 95% of individual observations lie within it

questions.explanation: CI reflects precision of the estimate; if a CI for a difference excludes 0 (or ratio excludes 1) the result is significant at 5%.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: A relative risk of 1.0 indicates:

options.B: No association between exposure and outcome

questions.explanation: RR >1 increased risk; RR <1 protective.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: In India, BCG vaccine is given at birth to prevent:
questions.explanation: BCG at birth (0.05 mL intradermal in the left upper arm); OPV zero dose at birth; Hepatitis B birth dose.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The measles-containing vaccine in the Indian national schedule is first given at:

questions.question: Oral polio vaccine is best stored at the primary vaccine store at:

questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: Herd immunity means that:

questions.explanation: It reduces transmission; the threshold depends on R0 (e.g. ~95% for measles).

questions.question: Pulmonary tuberculosis is mainly transmitted by:

questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The vector of malaria is the:

questions.question: The mosquito that transmits dengue breeds in:

questions.question: ORS stands for:

questions.question: Which route is the MOST important route of hepatitis B transmission?

questions.question: The earliest symptom of vitamin A deficiency is:

questions.question: Iodine deficiency disorders include:
questions.explanation: Iodised salt is the main control strategy.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The commonest nutritional deficiency in India among women is:
questions.explanation: IFA supplementation, deworming and dietary diversification form the national anaemia programme.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)

questions.question: The energy value of one gram of fat is:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate 4, protein 4, fat 9, alcohol 7 kcal per gram.

questions.question: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first:

questions.question: Rickets in children is due to deficiency of:

questions.question: The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) includes:

questions.question: Community-based rehabilitation (CBR) aims to:

questions.question: A ‘benchmark disability’ under the RPwD Act 2016 refers to:

questions.question: Silicosis is caused by inhalation of:

questions.question: Byssinosis is an occupational disease of workers exposed to:

questions.question: Ergonomics is the study of:

questions.question: The correct technique for lifting a heavy object from the floor is to:
